name: NCP163ASN280T1G
title: 250 mA ultra-low-noise, high-PSRR LDO regulator
summary: The NCP163 is a fixed-output 250 mA linear regulator built for RF and noise-sensitive analog loads: about 6.5 µVRMS of output noise, PSRR above 90 dB at low frequency, 12 µA quiescent current and 80 mV dropout at full load. It runs from 2.2 V to 5.5 V, is stable with 1 µF ceramic capacitors, and comes in two 0.35 mm-pitch WLCSP4 packages, a 1 mm XDFN4 and SOT23-5L. Versions differ in active output discharge and start-up ramp rate. NCP163ASN280T1G is the 2.8 V version A in SOT23-5L.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The regulator with a 1 µF ceramic capacitor from IN to ground and another from OUT to ground. EN is brought out as an on/off control input; the output feeds the load at VOUT.
notes: Pin NC exists on SOT23-5L only.

where.PD(MAX): largest power the part can dissipate, W
where.θJA: junction-to-ambient thermal resistance of the part on its board, °C/W

operation.text: A bandgap reference feeds an error amplifier whose output passes through an integrated soft-start stage to a driver with current limiting, which runs a PMOS pass transistor between IN and OUT. The die also holds enable logic and a thermal shutdown block. Version A adds an N-channel transistor from OUT to GND that the EN signal, through an inverter, switches on when the part is disabled.

Version A has the active output discharge and the normal start-up ramp; version B has no active discharge; version C has the active discharge and a slower start-up ramp. The family covers fixed outputs from 1.2 V to 5.3 V; orderable devices run from 1.2 V to 5.0 V, the set differing by package.
The regulator is protected against overload, a shorted output and over-temperature.

A capacitor at IN, placed as near the pin as possible, is needed for stability. Use X5R or X7R ceramic of 1 µF or more for the best dynamic behaviour across temperature. Its ESR is not constrained, but ceramic is preferred for low ESR and ESL; it shunts AC noise on the supply and lessens the effect of the supply wiring's inductance and resistance when the load steps.

OUT needs a capacitor placed close to the pin: 1 µF X5R or X7R is the recommended part, because these dielectrics change little with temperature. The loop stays stable down to 0.7 µF of effective capacitance, allowing for temperature, DC bias and case size. Very small cases such as 0201 lose capacitance quickly as DC bias rises. No minimum ESR applies; ESR must stay below 2 Ω. More capacitance and lower ESR can improve load transient response and high-frequency PSRR. Tantalum capacitors are not recommended at the output: their ESR is high and climbs at low temperature.

With EN below 0.4 V the part is off: the pass transistor is off, so almost no current flows from IN to OUT, and on version A the discharge transistor pulls OUT to GND through 280 Ω. Supply current when off is typically 10 nA. With EN above 1.2 V the part is on, regulates, and the discharge transistor is off. An internal pull-down of typically 200 nA holds the part off if EN is left open. When the enable function is not needed, EN should be tied directly to IN.

A built-in soft-start makes the output rise smoothly and monotonically after EN goes high, which keeps the input surge down when a large output capacitance is fitted. Two ramp rates exist: the normal ramp of the A option and a slower ramp of the C option.

Output current is limited inside the IC to typically 700 mA, measured where VOUT has fallen to 90 % of nominal. With a dead short at the output (VOUT = 0 V) the current is limited to typically 690 mA. Both limits work over the full temperature and input voltage ranges, and a short may last indefinitely.

When the die passes the shutdown threshold (typically 160 °C) the regulator turns off, and it stays off until the die cools below the reset threshold (typically 140 °C), when it turns on again. This guards against failure from accidental overheating and does not replace proper heat sinking.

How much power the part can dissipate depends on the board: pad layout, PCB material and ambient temperature all set how fast the junction heats. The maximum follows from θJA and the ambient temperature, and the actual dissipation from the input voltage, ground current and load; θJA falls and PD(MAX) rises as PCB copper area grows, for each package.
Inside the PMOS pass device is a body diode that conducts from OUT to IN whenever VOUT is above VIN. Where a lasting reverse condition can occur, external protection may be needed.
PSRR between 100 kHz and 10 MHz can be adjusted by the choice of output capacitor and by the PCB layout.

Turn-on time runs from EN going high until VOUT reaches 98 % of nominal, and depends on VOUT(NOM), COUT and TA. The specified turn-on times (120 µs for the A option, 135 µs for the C option, COUT = 1 µF) are measured to 95 % of VOUT(NOM).

Put CIN and COUT close to the pins and keep the traces wide for good transient response and regulation. 0402 or 0201 capacitors of suitable value keep the circuit small. More copper on the pins lowers thermal resistance, and the exposed pad can be joined to GND to spread heat and run the part cooler.
